1700	// headViewFactory builds a restricted BlockReader view of a portion of the head, covering the
1701	// closed time range [mint, maxt]. Implementations decide which subset of series the view exposes
1702	// (for example, by filtering on a list of series refs). The factory is invoked once per
1703	// chunk-range slice during compaction.
1704	type headViewFactory func(head *Head, mint, maxt int64) BlockReader
1705	
1706	// headSeriesEvictor removes from the head the series that were just
1707	// written to blocks without advancing HeadMinTime.
1708	//
1709	// The evictor must preserve any series that may have received samples
1710	// after compaction began, as those samples might not be present in the
1711	// generated blocks.
1712	//
1713	// maxt is the head's MaxTime at compaction start and is used to detect
1714	// obvious late writes via sample timestamps.
1715	//
1716	// appendIDWatermark is the head's append-ID counter at compaction
1717	// start. A series containing samples with appendID >
1718	// appendIDWatermark must not be evicted, as those samples were appended
1719	// after compaction began and may not be present in any block.
1720	//
1721	// When isolation is disabled, appendIDWatermark is always 0 and the
1722	// append-ID check becomes a no-op. In that mode, the caller must ensure
1723	// that no concurrent writes target the selected series.
1724	type headSeriesEvictor func(maxt int64, appendIDWatermark uint64) error
1725	
1726	// compactHeadViewLocked writes a block (or sequence of blocks, one per chunk range) for the
1727	// restricted head view produced by viewFactory, then runs evictor to remove those series from the
1728	// head. HeadMinTime is not advanced; series outside the view are unaffected. configure, if
1729	// non-nil, is called on the freshly created BlockMeta before each write to set compaction hints
1730	// or other optional fields.
1731	// The caller must hold db.cmtx.
1732	func (db *DB) compactHeadViewLocked(viewFactory headViewFactory, evict headSeriesEvictor, configure func(*BlockMeta)) error {
1733		mint, maxt := db.head.opts.ChunkRange*(db.head.MinTime()/db.head.opts.ChunkRange), db.head.MaxTime()
1734		// Capture the head's current append-ID as an eviction watermark before
1735		// writing any blocks.
1736		//
1737		// The generated blocks are guaranteed to contain all samples with
1738		// appendID <= watermark. Samples appended later (appendID > watermark)
1739		// may or may not be present, depending on when each block writer takes
1740		// its isolation snapshot.
1741		//
1742		// Eviction uses the watermark as a safety guard: a series is removed
1743		// only if it has not received any samples with appendID > watermark
1744		// since compaction began.
1745		appendIDWatermark := db.head.iso.lastAppendID()
1746		// The bound is inclusive so that a sample sitting exactly on a chunk-range boundary
1747		// (mint == maxt) still gets a block written before its series is evicted.
1748		for ; mint <= maxt; mint += db.head.chunkRange.Load() {
1749			view := viewFactory(db.head, mint, mint+db.head.chunkRange.Load()-1)
1750	
1751			meta := &BlockMeta{}
1752			if configure != nil {
1753				configure(meta)
1754			}
1755			uids, err := db.compactor.Write(db.dir, view, view.Meta().MinTime, view.Meta().MaxTime+1, meta)
1756			if err != nil {
1757				return fmt.Errorf("persist head portion: %w", err)
1758			}
1759	
1760			// compactor.Write returns no UIDs when the view contained no chunks, which happens
1761			// on a chunk-range slice that holds no data for the selected series. There is nothing
1762			// to reload or log in that case.
1763			if len(uids) == 0 {
1764				continue
1765			}
1766	
1767			db.logger.Info("Head portion block created", "ulids", fmt.Sprintf("%v", uids), "min_time", mint, "max_time", mint+db.head.chunkRange.Load()-1)
1768	
1769			if err := db.reloadBlocks(); err != nil {
1770				errs := []error{fmt.Errorf("reloadBlocks blocks: %w", err)}
1771				for _, uid := range uids {
1772					if errRemoveAll := os.RemoveAll(filepath.Join(db.dir, uid.String())); errRemoveAll != nil {
1773						errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("delete persisted head portion block after failed db reloadBlocks:%s: %w", uid, errRemoveAll))
1774					}
1775				}
1776				return errors.Join(errs...)
1777			}
1778		}
1779	
1780		if compactHeadViewBeforeEvictTestingCallback != nil {
1781			compactHeadViewBeforeEvictTestingCallback()
1782			compactHeadViewBeforeEvictTestingCallback = nil
1783		}
1784	
1785		if err := evict(maxt, appendIDWatermark); err != nil {
1786			return fmt.Errorf("head truncate: %w", err)
1787		}
1788		db.head.RebuildSymbolTable(db.logger)
1789	
1790		return nil
1791	}

units.headline: New helper reports whether a series has no OOO state
units.summary: Pulls the old `s.ooo != nil` check out of staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData into a one-line predicate. It is reused by the filter step and by both evict predicates. The logic is the same as before.
units.reason: Trivial predicate pulled out of existing logic; the risky uses are reviewed in other units.

units.headline: Stale-NaN check pulled into a reusable isStaleSeries helper
units.summary: Moves the stale-NaN check on float, histogram and float-histogram last values into a helper. The expression matches the removed inline code in gcStaleSeries and staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData exactly.
units.reason: Moved expression with clear equivalence to the removed inline code.

units.headline: Stale truncation now also requires no OOO data and no appends after the watermark
units.summary: truncateStaleSeries now hands a predicate to the generic truncateSeries. The predicate requires no OOO state, a stale last value, and no appendID above the watermark. Eviction for CompactStaleHead is therefore stricter than before, and its safety depends on how the watermark is captured.
focus: Watermark comes from iso.lastAppendID(), which counts appenders that are still open; their later commits are not caught
Series that gained OOO data after the ref list was collected are now kept, where before they could be evicted
units.reason: Changes which series get evicted and tombstoned in the WAL during stale-head compaction.

units.headline: New evictor removes selected series that have no OOO data or late appends
units.summary: Adds the eviction step for CompactSelectedSeries. It evicts every listed series with maxTime <= maxt, no OOO state and no appendID above the watermark, then writes WAL tombstones for them. Any sample missing from the block at that point is lost for good.
focus: Whether the appendID watermark really covers appenders that were open when it was captured
Isolation-disabled mode: the guard does nothing, so a late in-range sample is lost silently

issues.title: Appender opened before watermark but committed after block write gets evicted
issues.failure_scenario: Appender A gets appendID N and stays open. Compaction captures watermark = lastAppendID = N. The block is written while A's samples are still uncommitted, so they are not in the block. A then commits a sample with t <= maxt, which adds appendID N to s.txs. N > N is false, so the series is evicted and tombstoned, and the committed sample is lost from the head and from WAL replay.

units.reason: New code path that evicts series and writes WAL tombstones, so a wrong decision loses data.

units.headline: New check for appendIDs above a watermark in a series' tx ring
units.summary: Walks s.txs (the per-series append-ID ring) looking for any ID greater than the watermark, and returns false when isolation is off. This is the only guard against evicting samples that arrived during compaction. It works only if every sample with appendID <= watermark is already in the block.
focus: The watermark is lastAppendID, not the low watermark, so uncommitted appenders with ID <= watermark are not detected
Ring iteration bounds: txIDCount==0 with an empty slice

issues.title: Watermark comparison misses appends from appenders open before capture
issues.failure_scenario: An appendID handed out before compaction (so <= lastAppendID watermark) whose samples are committed only after the block snapshot. hasAppendIDAbove returns false, the series is evicted, and the newly committed in-range sample is lost. Comparing against the low watermark (lowest open appendID) instead would catch it.

units.reason: This guard decides whether committed samples survive eviction.

units.headline: Generic series truncation takes an eviction predicate and returns the deleted count
units.summary: truncateStaleSeries becomes truncateSeries: it takes a shouldEvict predicate, returns the number of evicted series, and calls gcSeries. Locking, waiting for readers and the WAL tombstone logic are unchanged. Every caller passes its own predicate.
focus: Callers ignore the new int return value; check nothing relies on it
shouldEvict runs inside gcSeries while the series lock is held
units.reason: Core eviction path refactored to take a predicate; it writes WAL tombstones.

units.headline: Test call updated for the new watermark argument
units.summary: Passes math.MaxUint64 as the watermark, which turns the appendID guard off. No assertions changed.
units.reason: Signature update in a test only; assertions are unchanged.

units.headline: New test for filterSeriesAndSortPostings with clean, OOO and bogus refs
units.summary: New test showing that the filter keeps a clean series, drops a series with OOO data, and drops a ref that does not exist. It cannot affect production behavior.
units.reason: New test only.

units.headline: New helper reports whether a series has no OOO state
units.summary: Pulls the old `s.ooo != nil` check out of staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData into a one-line predicate. It is reused by the filter step and by both evict predicates. The logic is the same as before.
units.reason: Trivial predicate pulled out of existing logic; the risky uses are reviewed in other units.

units.headline: Stale-NaN check pulled into a reusable isStaleSeries helper
units.summary: Moves the stale-NaN check on float, histogram and float-histogram last values into a helper. The expression matches the removed inline code in gcStaleSeries and staleSeriesRefsNoOOOData exactly.
units.reason: Moved expression with clear equivalence to the removed inline code.

units.headline: Stale truncation now also requires no OOO data and no appends after the watermark
units.summary: truncateStaleSeries now hands a predicate to the generic truncateSeries. The predicate requires no OOO state, a stale last value, and no appendID above the watermark. Eviction for CompactStaleHead is therefore stricter than before, and its safety depends on how the watermark is captured.
focus: Watermark comes from iso.lastAppendID(), which counts appenders that are still open; their later commits are not caught
Series that gained OOO data after the ref list was collected are now kept, where before they could be evicted
units.reason: Changes which series get evicted and tombstoned in the WAL during stale-head compaction.

units.headline: New evictor removes selected series that have no OOO data or late appends
units.summary: Adds the eviction step for CompactSelectedSeries. It evicts every listed series with maxTime <= maxt, no OOO state and no appendID above the watermark, then writes WAL tombstones for them. Any sample missing from the block at that point is lost for good.
focus: Whether the appendID watermark really covers appenders that were open when it was captured
Isolation-disabled mode: the guard does nothing, so a late in-range sample is lost silently

issues.title: Appender opened before watermark but committed after block write gets evicted
issues.failure_scenario: Appender A gets appendID N and stays open. Compaction captures watermark = lastAppendID = N. The block is written while A's samples are still uncommitted, so they are not in the block. A then commits a sample with t <= maxt, which adds appendID N to s.txs. N > N is false, so the series is evicted and tombstoned, and the committed sample is lost from the head and from WAL replay.

units.reason: New code path that evicts series and writes WAL tombstones, so a wrong decision loses data.

units.headline: New check for appendIDs above a watermark in a series' tx ring
units.summary: Walks s.txs (the per-series append-ID ring) looking for any ID greater than the watermark, and returns false when isolation is off. This is the only guard against evicting samples that arrived during compaction. It works only if every sample with appendID <= watermark is already in the block.
focus: The watermark is lastAppendID, not the low watermark, so uncommitted appenders with ID <= watermark are not detected
Ring iteration bounds: txIDCount==0 with an empty slice

issues.title: Watermark comparison misses appends from appenders open before capture
issues.failure_scenario: An appendID handed out before compaction (so <= lastAppendID watermark) whose samples are committed only after the block snapshot. hasAppendIDAbove returns false, the series is evicted, and the newly committed in-range sample is lost. Comparing against the low watermark (lowest open appendID) instead would catch it.

units.reason: This guard decides whether committed samples survive eviction.

units.headline: Generic series truncation takes an eviction predicate and returns the deleted count
units.summary: truncateStaleSeries becomes truncateSeries: it takes a shouldEvict predicate, returns the number of evicted series, and calls gcSeries. Locking, waiting for readers and the WAL tombstone logic are unchanged. Every caller passes its own predicate.
focus: Callers ignore the new int return value; check nothing relies on it
shouldEvict runs inside gcSeries while the series lock is held
units.reason: Core eviction path refactored to take a predicate; it writes WAL tombstones.

units.headline: Test call updated for the new watermark argument
units.summary: Passes math.MaxUint64 as the watermark, which turns the appendID guard off. No assertions changed.
units.reason: Signature update in a test only; assertions are unchanged.

units.headline: New test for filterSeriesAndSortPostings with clean, OOO and bogus refs
units.summary: New test showing that the filter keeps a clean series, drops a series with OOO data, and drops a ref that does not exist. It cannot affect production behavior.
units.reason: New test only.
